evals.name: write-live-log-view
evals.prompt: Implement mountLogView in evals/fixtures/log-viewer/src/log-view.ts. It should show the feed live with the newest line at the bottom, keep at most the last 10,000 lines, follow the bottom unless I scrolled up to read older lines, and return a cleanup function. The feed pushes about 500 lines per second.
evals.expected_output: A mountLogView implementation that batches feed lines into one DOM update per frame, keeps a bounded buffer and a bounded or virtualized DOM, avoids per-line layout reads, writes text without HTML parsing, tears everything down, and ends with a short Performance notes block.
expectations: Feed lines are buffered and applied to the DOM at most once per animation frame, not once per message (DATA-06, EVT-03)
The stored lines are capped at 10,000 with eviction of the oldest lines (LIFE-05)
The DOM stays bounded: rows are virtualized or capped, so the page never holds 10,000+ row elements (DOM-02 or DOM-01)
No layout read (scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, getBoundingClientRect) happens between DOM writes for single lines; at most one read, then the writes, per frame (EVT-07)
Line text is written with textContent or Text nodes, not innerHTML per line (DOM-04 or DOM-07)
The returned cleanup unsubscribes the feed, cancels any pending requestAnimationFrame, and removes scroll listeners (LIFE-01)
The answer ends with a 'Performance notes' block of at most 4 bullets in the '<Stage> (<rule>): <choice>. Cost: <trade-off>.' form, and says 'Not measured' with a recipe
No new dependency is added

evals.name: write-streaming-scichart
evals.prompt: In evals/fixtures/sensor-chart/src/sensor-chart.ts, stream the sensor feed into the SciChart line chart and keep the last 5 minutes visible. Messages are JSON {t, v} and can reach about 300 per second.
evals.expected_output: Streaming code that parses and buffers messages, appends once per frame with appendRange into a fifoCapacity series sized for 5 minutes at peak rate, declares the data flags, keeps time values in float64, moves the visible X window, and deletes the surface on teardown.
expectations: The data series uses fifoCapacity sized for 5 minutes at the peak message rate, with the arithmetic shown (SC-02)
Messages are buffered and appended once per frame with appendRange, not with append per message (SC-01, SC-02)
The series declares dataIsSortedInX, and containsNaN when the data has no NaN (SC-03)
Time values stay float64 in the axis unit; no Float32Array or float32 conversion of Unix-ms times (SC-05, DATA-05, GPU-14)
The visible X range follows the last 5 minutes through visibleRange or an equivalent auto-range setting (SC-43)
Teardown unsubscribes the feed, cancels the frame loop, and calls delete() on the surface exactly once (SC-28, LIFE-01)
The answer checks API names against the installed SciChart typings, or says they could not be checked, instead of trusting memory
The answer ends with a 'Performance notes' block that says 'Not measured' with a recipe

evals.name: review-product-grid
evals.prompt: Can you review evals/fixtures/product-grid (index.html, product-grid.ts, product-grid.css) for performance before I merge?
evals.expected_output: A review report in the references/review.md template: at most 10 findings grouped by pipeline stage, strongest first, each with severity, an evidence label, a fix and a Verify line. No code edits.
expectations: Finds the lazy-loaded hero (LCP) image and asks for fetchpriority="high" without loading="lazy", plus a reserved size (MEDIA-02, MEDIA-04)
Finds the synchronous analytics script in the head and asks for defer, async or a later load (HTML-04 or HTML-18)
Finds the CSS @import and asks for a <link> (HTML-07)
Finds the hover animation of top and box-shadow and asks for transform and opacity, with a pre-painted shadow layer (CSS-01, CSS-02)
Finds will-change: transform on every card (CSS-05)

Finds the scroll handler that reads getBoundingClientRect for every card and writes styles on every scroll event, and proposes IntersectionObserver or one rAF with reads before writes (EVT-07, EVT-11)
Finds grid.innerHTML += inside the loop and the per-card click listeners, and proposes building once and one delegated listener (DOM-07 or DOM-06, EVT-10)
Finds the full-size product images without srcset, sizes or lazy loading below the fold (MEDIA-03, MEDIA-05)
Finds the resize listener that re-renders the whole grid and the listeners that are never removed (LIFE-01)
Findings are grouped by pipeline stage with severity and M, S or H evidence labels, each with a fix and a Verify line; no fixture file is edited

evals.name: measure-side-panel
evals.prompt: I switched the side panel open/close from a height transition to a transform. evals/fixtures/side-panel/before.html is the old version and after.html is the new one. Is it actually smoother now? Serve the folder on localhost and measure it.
evals.expected_output: A measured answer: the same lab profile for both pages, scripted toggles, several interleaved runs per side, probes and a trace, compare-runs.mjs, and a verdict with numbers, device, profile, build and run count. No claim without data.
expectations: Runs a preflight of the Chrome DevTools MCP tools, or stops and says which tool is missing
Serves the folder on 127.0.0.1 and applies one lab profile (CPU throttling and viewport) to both pages
Drives the toggle with a script (window.togglePanel) the same way on both pages, with at least 5 interleaved runs per side or a stated reason for fewer
Uses the frame probe from scripts/probes.js and/or a saved trace, and checks whether the height transition runs on the main thread (non-composited animation, Layout per frame)
Compares the runs with scripts/compare-runs.mjs and reports the verdict with numbers, the device, the profile, the build and the run count
Says 'smoother' only if the numbers beat the noise band; a neutral result is reported as neutral
Does not edit before.html or after.html, and stops the local server and closes the pages at the end
